name: Dependency updates and audits
needs: GitHub says my packages have vulnerabilities
keep my npm packages up to date
a library I use has a security hole
summary: A routine for keeping third-party packages current and checked against known vulnerabilities: pinned versions in a lockfile, automatic update pull requests, and an audit step that fails the build on serious issues.
need_when: Your app uses packages from npm, PyPI or any registry, which is nearly every app.
skip_when: Never. Throwaway prototypes can skip the routine, not the lockfile.

ways.title: Dependabot
ways.how: Turn on Dependabot alerts and security updates, and add a dependabot.yml for weekly version updates.
ways.tradeoff: Built in. Can open a lot of pull requests unless you group them.

ways.title: Renovate
ways.how: The Renovate app or self-hosted runner opens grouped update pull requests with automerge rules for safe updates.
ways.tradeoff: Very configurable. The config takes some learning.

ways.title: Audit commands in CI
ways.how: npm audit --audit-level=high, pip-audit, osv-scanner or bundler-audit run on every push.
ways.tradeoff: Catches known issues before deploy. Doesn't update anything for you.

prompt:
Set up dependency updates and vulnerability audits for this repo.

Requirements:
- Make sure every dependency is pinned in a committed lockfile.
- Add [Dependabot / Renovate] config: weekly, grouped minor and patch updates, separate pull requests for majors, security updates right away.
- Add CI steps: [npm audit --audit-level=high], [pip-audit -r requirements.txt] (or osv-scanner for both). Fail the build on high or critical.
- Tests must run on update pull requests. Automerge only patch updates that pass.
- Document how to handle an audit failure with no fix yet (pin, replace, or record an exception with an expiry date).
- List current high and critical findings and fix or explain each.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. Adding a package with a known high vulnerability fails CI.
2. An update pull request appears within a week and runs the tests.
3. Every dependency file has a lockfile next to it.
4. Current audit output has no unexplained high or critical findings.
5. Exceptions have an owner and expiry date.
acceptance_checks: Adding a package with a known high vulnerability fails CI.
An update pull request appears within a week and runs the tests.
Every dependency file has a lockfile next to it.
Current audit output has no unexplained high or critical findings.
Exceptions have an owner and expiry date.
if_you_skip_it: A known hole in an old package stays in production for months, or a year of skipped updates turns into one painful upgrade.
how_derek_runs_it: Custody Journal's release gate runs pip-audit against requirements.txt and npm audit with --audit-level=high on its lockfiles, and the release stops if either fails.
